primary.thesis: Hyperbeat is a vault and yield protocol on HyperEVM, the Hyperliquid ecosystem. It has a points program and a seed round from well-known investors. It has good reason to hold its TGE (token launch) before the end of 2026, while Hyperliquid-ecosystem attention is still high and before points farmers lose interest. I expect the token to launch by the deadline. Airdrop-driven launches of mid-tier DeFi infrastructure tokens usually settle at a day-1 FDV of tens of millions to low hundreds of millions of dollars. The float is thin and early price discovery is noisy, and airdrop recipients sell on the first day, which usually caps the FDV below the valuations seen at the top of the cycle. So the likeliest result is a launch whose day-1 FDV clears $50M but stays below $300M.

basket.reason: If the token launches at all, a protocol with real TVL, known backers and an active points community rarely prices below $50M FDV on day one. The main risk is that there is no launch.
Selling by airdrop recipients and a mid-tier comparable set should keep the day-1 FDV below $300M. This contract also pays if the token does not launch by 31 Dec 2026.
$400M+ would take a Hyperliquid-mania repricing. This contract also wins if the launch slips past the deadline, so it partly offsets C3's risk of no launch.

failure_narrative: There are two ways to lose. (a) Hyperbeat does not make its token actively and publicly tradable by 31 Dec 2026, 11:59 PM ET. It might delay the TGE because crypto markets are weak, because of legal or listing timing, or because it wants to run the points season longer. C3 then resolves NO while C6 and C7 pay, so the loss is partial. (b) The token launches during a strong Hyperliquid/HYPE rally. Enough of the supply is locked, the float is low, and major exchange listings plus a HYPE-denominated wealth effect push the day-1 FDV above $300-400M, so C6 and C7 both lose. The worst case is a hot launch in a strong Hyperliquid market.
hedge_thesis: The hedge covers the Hyperliquid ecosystem as a whole: the HYPE token price, activity on HyperEVM, and TGE valuations of other Hyperliquid-native projects. Branch (b) of the failure happens when the Hyperliquid ecosystem is richly valued. HYPE is up, HyperEVM TVL and airdrop wealth are high, and new ecosystem tokens list at high FDVs. So instruments that pay when HYPE rises or when other HyperEVM tokens launch at high valuations would tend to pay in exactly the worlds where Hyperbeat blows through $300M. Branch (a), a delayed launch, is already offset by C6 and C7. The mechanism is shared beta: Hyperbeat's day-1 valuation mostly reflects Hyperliquid-ecosystem risk appetite and HYPE-denominated liquidity, not anything specific to the protocol.
